questions.q_en: Who discovered radioactivity?
questions.solution_en:
• Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 while working with phosphorescent materials.

• Marie Curie and Pierre Curie further researched radioactivity and discovered radium and polonium.

• Ernest Rutherford contributed to the study of radioactive decay and atomic structure.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements regarding alpha (α) particles is correct?

(a) They have high penetrating power.

(b) They have a charge of +2e.

(c) Their emission increases the atomic number of an element.
questions.solution_en:
• Alpha particles are helium nuclei with a +2e charge.

• Alpha particles have low penetrating power.

• Alpha decay decreases the atomic number.

• Alpha particles

○ Composition: Consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons (Helium nucleus).

○ Emission: Released during alpha decay of heavy nuclei.

○ Charge & Mass: Positively charged (+2) and relatively heavy.

○ Speed: Moves at approximately 10⁷ m/s.

○ Ionization: Highly ionizing, causing significant damage in a short path.

○ Penetration: Low penetrating power; stopped by paper or a few cm of air.

○ Biological Effect: Harmful if inhaled or ingested, causing severe tissue damage.

○ Scattering: Deflected when passing through thin metal foils.

questions.q_en: The half-life of a radioactive substance is the time in which:
options_en: The mass of the substance reduces to zero
The mass reduces to half of its initial value
The atomic number reduces by half
questions.solution_en:
• Half-life is the time taken for half of a radioactive sample to decay.

• Decay of mass never reaches zero.

• Atomic numbers may not always be halved.

• Decay continues indefinitely.

• Half life of radio active substance

○ The time taken for half of a radioactive substance to decay is known as Half life of radioactive

○ Nature: It is constant for a given radioactive substance

○ Dependence: Independent of the initial amount of the substance.

○ Measurement: Expressed in seconds, minutes, hours, years, etc.

○ Application: Used in carbon dating, nuclear medicine, and nuclear waste management.

○ Example: Uranium-238 has a half-life of 4.5 billion years.

questions.q_en: Which of the following types of radiation has the highest penetrating power?
questions.solution_en:
• Gamma rays have the highest penetration power.

• Alpha has the lowest penetration.

• Beta is moderate.

• X-rays are less penetrating than gamma rays.

• Gamma Rays

○ Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic waves emitted from the nucleus of a radioactive atom.

○ They have no mass and no charge, unlike alpha and beta particles.

○ Highly penetrating; can pass through most materials except dense substances like lead or thick concrete.

○ Usually emitted along with alpha or beta decay to release excess nuclear energy.

○ Travel at the speed of light (3 x 108m/s) in a vacuum.

○ Detected using devices like Geiger-Muller counters and scintillation detectors.

○ Weakly ionizing compared to alpha and beta particles.

○ Widely used in cancer radiotherapy, sterilization, food preservation, and industrial imaging.

○ Requires heavy elements like lead or several meters of concrete for effective shielding.

questions.q_en:
Which among the following statements is NOT true about beta (β) decay?

(a) It involves the emission of electrons or positrons.

(b) It results in an increase or decrease in atomic number.

(c) It emits helium nuclei.
questions.solution_en:
• Beta decay does not emit helium nuclei (which are α particles).

• Beta Decay

○ Beta decay is a type of radioactive decay in which a nucleus emits a beta particle (electron or positron).

○ It occurs in two forms - Beta-minus (β⁻) decay and Beta-plus (β⁺) decay.

○ Beta-minus (β⁻) Decay: A neutron converts into a proton, emitting an electron (e-) and an antineutrino

○ Beta-plus (β⁺) Decay: A proton converts into a neutron, emitting a positron (e+) and a neutrino.

○ More penetrating than alpha particles but less than gamma rays; can be stopped by a few millimeters of aluminum.

○ Moderate ionizing ability, higher than gamma rays but lower than alpha particles.

○ The mass number remains unchanged in beta decay

○ Used in medical treatments (e.g., radiotherapy), carbon dating (C14 decay), and nuclear reactors.

questions.q_en: The isotope used in carbon dating is:
questions.solution_en:
• Carbon-14 is used in radiocarbon dating.

• Carbon dating is a method used to determine the age of ancient organic materials.

• It is based on the radioactive decay of Carbon-14 (C-14) isotope.

• Half-life of C-14: Approximately 5730 years.

• Living organisms absorb C-14 from the atmosphere; after death, C-14 decays at a known rate.

• Used in archaeology, geology, and paleontology to date fossils, wood, and artifacts up to 50,000 years old.

questions.solution_en:

• Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from unstable atomic nuclei.

• Cause: Occurs due to nuclear instability, leading to decay into a more stable nucleus.

• Half-Life: The time taken for half of a radioactive substance to decay.

• Units of Measurement: Measured in Becquerel (Bq) and Curie (Ci).

questions.q_en: Which of the following is correct regarding the energy released in radioactive decay?
options_en: It is equal to the mass defect multiplied by the square of the speed of light.
It is always greater than the energy released in a chemical reaction.
It depends on the binding energy per nucleon of the daughter nucleus.

questions.q_en: In nuclear fission, the binding energy per nucleon of the daughter nuclei is:
options_en: Lower than that of the parent nucleus
Equal to that of the parent nucleus
Higher than that of the parent nucleus
questions.solution_en:
• The products of fission have a higher binding energy per nucleon, which makes them more stable and releases energy in the process.

• Nuclear fission is the process in which a heavy nucleus splits into two or more smaller nuclei, releasing a large amount of energy.

• A tremendous amount of heat and radiation is released due to the breaking of nuclear bonds.

• A single fission reaction releases neutrons, which further cause more fission, leading to a self-sustaining reaction.

questions.q_en: Heavy water (D₂O) is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors because it:
questions.solution_en:
• Heavy water reduces the speed of fast neutrons, increasing the probability of fission in nuclear reactors.

• A moderator is a substance used in a nuclear reactor to slow down fast neutrons, making them more likely to sustain a controlled fission reaction.

• Common Moderators: Heavy water (D₂O), Graphite, Light water (H₂O), Beryllium, and Carbon.

• Reduces the speed of neutrons without absorbing them, increasing the probability of Uranium-235 or Plutonium-239 undergoing fission.
